SpaceX last year acquired $2.6 billion worth of spectrum licenses from EchoStar to improve its Starlink network's 5G connections.

tech.title: What Is Quantum Advantage Actually Worth?
tech.summary: Nearly all roadmaps point to a utility-scale quantum computer being developed around 2030. Despite this, there is little confidence or clarity on how these machines will actually be useful. The consensus is now that they'll first be used for breaking cryptography. The second most concrete answer is to use them to generate simulation data for AI labs' science models. This post looks at how else quantum computing could be applied and where all the revenue will come from.

tech.title: China publicly discloses plan for a lunar landing within three years
tech.summary: Chinese space officials have confirmed the country's plans to land astronauts on the Moon within three years. The landings will involve a lunar-orbit rendezvous similar to what NASA did with the Apollo program. China and the US are racing to land astronauts on the lunar surface, as it would be a major geopolitical win. Both countries are also building capabilities to establish a long-term presence at the Moon's South Pole.

tech.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI

Its technical staff built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches and to maximize read throughput. The team implemented the backend without interrupting any engineering work or changing how the team uses Git. Pando cut median push latency in production by nearly 5x, and it now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.

tech.title: Why Agents Are Soon Only Going to Have 1 Tool
tech.summary: Agents are collapsing their entire tool catalog into one 'exec' tool. This allows models to write short scripts that chain, combine, and await actions inside isolated sandboxes. Models can now reliably combine and chain dependent actions in a single pass. In the previous standard tool-calling model, agents could only perform single actions, but the exec tool allows them to perform multiple actions.

tech.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside
tech.summary: Organizations are losing attention as everyone within is doing something they think is useful, but all that work draws on the same limited capacity to understand, review, and decide. Just because work exists doesn't mean it's the right thing to do. Output is not proof of value. A working implementation only means that something can be built, not that it should be - some changes have negative value.

tech.title: The value of open source
tech.summary: People open source projects for various reasons. Some do it to build a company or product, others do it performatively, and some ship code just for the love of the game. Open source was never free to copy, and the code was never the moat. AI can remake a product, but it can't provide the rest of the value a company generates. The technology is helping maintainers ship and fix problems faster.

The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.

ai.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands

One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

infosec.title: Fashion retailer Resolve says hackers stole payment card information

Texas regulators recorded 127,200 affected residents. Vermont reported 1,328. Revolve notified law enforcement, hired a cybersecurity firm, and said operations and finances were unaffected.

infosec.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
infosec.summary: A suspected cyber-attack switched refrigeration evaporators to defrost mode at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland. Freezer temperatures reportedly reached 50°C, forcing stores to discard spoiled food. A Delhaize branch reported €100,000 in losses. Sabcobel said affected units need physical changes. Remote internet-connected maintenance remains part of the operating model.

infosec.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
infosec.summary: IBM reported four Langflow vulnerabilities affecting versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8. Two are critical and require no account: CVE-2026-93680 bypasses authentication, while CVE-2026-110186 permits arbitrary code execution through MCP tool enumeration. A public Metasploit module already enumerates Langflow MCP tools without credentials. Version 1.13.0 is the only fix. It disables automatic login by default. IBM has not published a workaround.

infosec.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
infosec.summary: Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP requests in Q3 2026. Short attacks under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps rose 208% year over year, while attacks above 1 Tbps fell 69% from Q2. CLDAP floods dropped 99.5%. DNS amplification rose 215%, and UDP floods rose 122%. The United States was the most-attacked country, followed by China and Indonesia. Canada rose from 16th to 6th, and Israel to 10th. IoT botnets remain active, with Mirai-classified traffic peaking at 57.23 PB in August.

infosec.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
infosec.summary: Researchers at Parameter Labs discovered a complex attack chain that could let attackers create malicious pages using ChatGPT's HTML Previews (formerly Canvas). The exploit begins by using the MathLive JavaScript library to create a new iframe that could load scripts from YouTube despite OpenAI's CSP policy. That iframe could then use YouTube's oEmbed endpoint to access OpenAI API endpoints and steal private data from anyone who accesses the ChatGPT share URL.

infosec.title: Turning the Valve - Exploiting RCE and LPE in the Steam Platform
infosec.summary: Atredis researchers found four local privilege escalation flaws and two remote code execution bugs in Steam for Windows. The LPE paths abused Steam's SYSTEM service through install-script allowlists, module loading, secure-desktop input forwarding, and driver installation. The remote bugs affected Steam-to-Steam synchronization messages: stack overflows in download-schedule and app-status handlers, plus an uninitialized-memory leak of steamclient64 pointers. The researchers combined the leak with an overflow to build a zero-click RCE using a ROP chain. They reported the issues to Valve through HackerOne. The bugs are patched or past the disclosure timeline, and proof-of-concept code is public.

infosec.title: AI is accelerating software development. Attackers are accelerating, too.
infosec.summary: Digital.ai's 2026 App Security Threat Report examines how AI is changing attack economics. 87% of monitored applications faced active attacks in 2026, up from 57% in 2023. One application experienced an attack just 1 hour and 56 minutes after appearing in an app store. Is your AppSec strategy keeping up? Read the report.

infosec.title: Wake and Break
infosec.summary: Wake and Break is a PSP (Platform Security Processor) exploit for AMD navi31 cards that will disable PSP's firmware signature check so that the card will load unsigned IP firmware.

infosec.title: MCPTrace

infosec.title: Securing Internet Critical Software: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash
infosec.summary: Researchers at Hacktron discovered a command injection vulnerability in GNU Savannah that let them gain root and take over user accounts, including a Bash maintainer. The vulnerability stemmed from the GPG key validator inserting a user's email address directly into commands it executed without sanitizing the input. The attackers utilized this vulnerability to install a webshell, read the database password, set their account to a superuser, impersonate other users, and also escalate privileges by exploiting GemOver(lay).

infosec.title: Cyberattack Hits Rosstat as Hackers Claim Huge Data Theft
infosec.summary: The Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow hacking groups claimed they stole 23TB of data from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat. The attackers claim to have stolen data on Russian wartime losses, demographic and economic statistics, and documents marked “for official use only.” Rosstat denied that any databases or legally protected information was leaked.

Chrome also implemented LLM-based ClickFix attack detection.

design.title: Canva Unveils Brush, an AI Model Built to Edit Designs at Lower Cost
design.summary: Brush, Canva's in-house vision-language model, edits designs up to 69% faster than the previous design agent at 46% lower cost per task. It reads both content and layout across full designs like multi-page decks, writes and runs small pieces of code, and inspects results before each next step. Brush is in beta for Canva Pro subscribers, with Brand Kit support and better image-heavy layout handling planned.

design.title: Amstel Updates Global Visual Identity to Highlight Amsterdam Heritage
design.summary: Amstel has redesigned its packaging and logo around its 1870 Amsterdam origins, adding bespoke typography inspired by historic canal bridge signage and a refined golden circle. The red, white, black, and gold system also features a wave pattern, a horizontal split evoking the Amstel River, and three coins representing the founders, city, and waterway. Already a Red Dot winner, the identity is rolling out across 11 markets, with all remaining territories due to transition by the end of 2027.

design.title: Design is more than creation
design.summary: Design is the deliberate process of deciding how something should work, respond, and be experienced, not simply the act of producing something that looks convincing. Conditions such as accessibility needs, localization, unpredictable content, failures, and different input methods should shape software from the beginning rather than being treated as edge cases to fix afterward. AI makes polished software dramatically faster to create, but that speed increases the importance of understanding which decisions were made, which assumptions they rely on, and whether they survive contact with reality.

design.title: How We're Training a Figma-Fluent Editing Model
design.summary: Specialized post-training lets Figma's first-party editing model compete with frontier models on precise, iterative edits to existing designs. A Llama 3.3 70B model trained on 250,000+ examples first became competitive with top models, but imitation learning limited generalization, so Figma now invests in reinforcement learning. Since beta, typical tasks run about 20% faster, users rate results 33% higher, and they undo the agent's work 60% less often.

design.title: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience”
design.summary: AI agents complicate the traditional definition of UX because people may increasingly accomplish goals without directly interacting with the companies, applications, and interfaces involved. Experience design provides a broader framing that includes traditional UX while also considering digital systems used by agents acting on humans' behalf and journeys involving multiple human and nonhuman actors. People's goals remain central, but designers must now consider experiences in which the immediate user of a product may be an AI rather than a person.

design.title: Can AI Agents Use Your Product?
design.summary: Dedica tests your site the way AI agents use it, then gives your team a fix for every place they fail.

design.title: Apple Dimensional Drawings
design.summary: Download dimensional drawings and technical specifications to help you design for Apple devices.

design.title: In the Age of AI, Curiosity is Our Greatest Creative Tool
design.summary: AI makes generating images and concepts easy, so the harder work is deciding what is worth making, whose perspective is missing, and whether it communicates. At DesignThinkers, RGD's annual conference in Toronto, speakers covered information design, blending strategy with creativity, and designing a city. AI-accelerated trends risk polished sameness, so "raw, messy curiosity is the most valuable thing we can bring to the table."

design.title: How to Write Better Copy for Graphic Design Projects
design.summary: Better graphic design copy starts with the project's purpose: a plain-language explanation, the audience, the most relevant benefit, objections, and the desired next step. Specific details persuade where vague praise does not, and a consistent brand voice should sound like the owner speaking face to face. Copy must fit its space, CTAs must match the reader's decision stage, and a final proofread should test every link and QR code.

design.title: Studio Kiln designs an identity for Reset that adapts like its app
design.summary: Studio Kiln's identity for Reset reflects the weight-loss app's personalized approach to eating, building flexibility and responsiveness directly into its visual system. A dynamic identity uses typography, color, imagery, and graphic elements that can shift across different contexts while maintaining a recognizable core. The result gives Reset a distinctive presence without locking a product built around personalized meal guidance into a rigid visual language.

design.title: The Window with No Buttons
design.summary: Style Dictionary, Storybook, and AI coding agents all run from the terminal, a blank window that feels like a wall to designers used to canvases.

design.title: French Concept Artist Uses Razor-Sharp Shapes and Neon Colors to Create the Most Dynamic Characters You Will See Today
design.summary: François Bourdin, a French freelance concept artist, character designer, and illustrator in Nantes, creates dynamic characters from razor-sharp angular linework and vivid, saturated neon palettes.

marketing.title: You don't need to be an SEO expert to grow through your website.
marketing.summary: Organic growth gets talked about like a technical project. Keywords, rankings, AI visibility scores. For most teams, it's overwhelming. Start with a simpler question: what are your buyers asking? Answer those questions well on your website and you give Google and AI the answer to share with buyers. GrowthX learns your business, maps the questions your buyers ask, and turns them into content that gets published, measured and improved. SEO, AI visibility, content workflows and reporting, all in one platform. Learn more and see where to start.

marketing.title: Google says AI chatbots are hurting its bottom line
marketing.summary: Google's AI search features are putting pressure on its core advertising business. Search volume growth slowed from 19% in Q1 to 12% in Q3 while search revenue remained flat. Google says AI Mode queries generate less ad revenue and plans to expand ads across AI Overviews and AI Mode to offset the impact. As more users turn to chatbots for answers, Google faces a challenge in maintaining ad revenue while investing in increasingly costly AI features.

marketing.title: Can Advertising Fund Free AI? Evidence from ChatGPT's International Advertising Rollout
marketing.summary: ChatGPT's current advertising model cannot yet fund free access because its ads deliver less value to advertisers than established search channels. Ads reduced organic referral traffic by 6% to 8%, but conversion rates remained unchanged at 2.21%. Paid ChatGPT visitors generated $0.89 in revenue per session compared with $2.45 for Google Search and converted at less than a third of the rate. ChatGPT would need to lower ad prices substantially to compete with Google and make its free tier financially sustainable.

marketing.title: Low-hanging fruit for demand gen: Offer-focused image ads
marketing.summary: Drive Q4 sales with offer-focused Google Demand Gen image ads promoting deals like free gifts or limited-time drops. Use a simple layout that puts the product front and center alongside its biggest benefit and a high-contrast offer badge. Highlight 3-6 features, then test benefit-driven and curiosity-driven headlines. Descriptions can expand on the benefits or reinforce the deal with social proof.

marketing.title: Substack is a $0 cheat code for your brand
marketing.summary: Substack can send a newsletter roughly 50X more subscribers than Google, since every signup surfaces a few newsletters the writer recommends. Companies are tapping that loop with behind-the-scenes posts from the people building the product. PostHog recommends 10 engineering newsletters that all recommend it back, while Ramp gets a recommendation from TBPN's Substack as part of its sponsorship. Substack's audience stats rank which newsletters already share a brand's readers, pointing to the best swap partners.

marketing.title: Algos Wiki
marketing.summary: Algos.wiki is an unofficial, AI-powered encyclopedia of Instagram's algorithm that organizes information from platform announcements and leadership interviews into searchable topics. Use it to research how content is ranked and recommended, including how posting times and shares affect reach. It also tracks algorithm updates and links to supporting sources.

marketing.title: 6 App Growth Annual workshops you can watch for free (+ presenter slides)
marketing.summary: RevenueCat has made 6 App Growth Annual workshops free to watch, with presenter slides and handouts. Sessions cover mining customer feedback to write higher-converting copy and researching users to drive organic downloads. Others show how to use competitor ads to create AI-generated creatives and automate Meta ad research and optimization with AI.

marketing.title: Reach is not Proof
marketing.summary: Retailer-owned shopping agents have the strongest evidence of sales impact, while ChatGPT and Google have massive reach but no published purchase results. Amazon reports nearly $12B in incremental annualized sales from its assistant, while Walmart says Sparky users spend 40% more per order. Brands should make product data complete and accessible so agents can accurately evaluate and recommend their products. AI-driven discovery is already happening, but sales impact remains unproven across most categories.

marketing.title: Creator Sponsorship Prices Are Negotiated Upward From a Low First Offer, Data Shows
marketing.summary: Creator sponsorship deals often close well above a brand's first offer, which averaged just 27% of the creator's quoted price across 124 negotiations. Creators can negotiate higher rates by adjusting deliverables rather than cutting prices and using average views and CPMs to justify fees. Paid usage adds 30-40% to the rate. Longer-term partnerships also provide more predictable income while helping creators reduce reliance on one-off sponsorships.

marketing.title: When Bundling Hurts the Bottom Line
marketing.summary: When demand far outstrips inventory, selling items separately beats package deals and earns nearly as much as the best possible bundling mix. Bundling works with ample stock because it averages out how much each buyer values each item, widening the customer base. Under scarcity, that same averaging caps how high a bundle can be priced, while separate prices capture each item's top bidders. Selling separately can start to win once available inventory falls below about 30-60% of potential customers.

marketing.summary: A founder shares his Reddit growth strategy, from content creation to building trust without hard-selling.

marketing.title: What Reddit's Q3 earnings mean for marketers amid major traffic shift
marketing.summary: Reddit's referral traffic is falling by over 1M visits per week as Google's AI Overviews reduce clicks to the platform.

marketing.title: ‘The content creator election': digital streamers and TV networks face off for midterms coverage
marketing.summary: Former TV journalists are launching independent election-night livestreams on YouTube and Substack, challenging traditional networks as creator-led news gains traction.

founders.title: How AI Applications Earn Their Premium
founders.summary: Execution, context, proof, and pricing together strengthen the case for buying. Reliable work and trusted context create an advantage. Clear evidence makes value visible, and pricing lets customers share in efficiency gains while rewarding the vendor for improving delivery. Advantages must widen fast for applications to keep earning their premiums.

founders.title: The McDonaldization of Venture Capital
founders.summary: A bigger venture fund can change which version of your company an investor wants to back. Venture is splitting between firms seeking exceptional returns and asset managers built to deploy enormous pools of money. Large asset managers can be satisfied doubling or tripling their money, so they favor companies that can absorb billions of dollars in familiar markets. The same incentives push founders toward businesses that fit the next large investor's expectations.

founders.title: Building a growth engine with AI agents
founders.summary: Growth is becoming an engineering problem. This post presents a case study of agent-led growth for growth marketing teams experimenting with AI agents. It covers the experiments the team shipped, what worked, and what went wrong. Not everything needs to scale, and not every problem needs AI.

founders.title: When the models catch up
founders.summary: If the promised outcome depends on future model improvements, start with the work customers can finish today. Products that only demonstrate what might be possible can generate excitement, but back it up with evidence about what customers can finish today, as people pay for what they can accomplish. A useful partial solution can help you gain valuable feedback for the next model iteration. Keep in mind what the business can still offer when competitors can buy access to the same model.

founders.title: Introducing Monitors v2
founders.summary: Exa Monitors watches the web and delivers only what's new to agents at a chosen interval. It covers Exa's entire index of 211 million businesses, 3.2 million podcast episodes, 1.27 billion product listings, and over 130 million web pages, and only calls agents when something actually changes. Results are published to a webhook, so agents never have to poll. Monitors v2 drops the price of monitors 7x to $2 per 1,000 runs.

founders.title: People data for AI agents
founders.summary: Firecrawl provides people data for AI agents. It helps agents find, enrich, or verify professional contacts and high-intent audiences. The service connects to 12 people providers, each callable through the same Firecrawl API key. It can be used for deep research, smarter AI chats, AI agent tools, onboarding, lead enrichment, and much more.

founders.title: Innovate on your own business terms: Google Cloud spend caps now generally available
founders.summary: Google Cloud spend caps now pause eligible services without deleting resources. Caps for AI services trigger within minutes using estimated costs, while reserved Provisioned Throughput keeps running. Teams can apply caps automatically to new sandbox projects through the API and choose whether blocked services resume each month or wait for manual approval.

founders.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside
founders.summary: Organizations are losing attention as everyone within is doing something they think is useful, but all that work draws on the same limited capacity to understand, review, and decide. Just because work exists doesn't mean it's the right thing to do. Output is not proof of value. A working implementation only means that something can be built, not that it should be - some changes have negative value.

founders.title: What channels grow when organic search shrinks?
founders.summary: An email audience is becoming more valuable as organic search sends fewer visitors. An analysis of Similarweb data puts US email traffic up 16.3% in the first eight months of 2026 against the same period last year. Email added more visits than paid search after excluding Google's ad-routing domain, and the median website's email traffic grew 14.7%. The gains include receipts and notifications, so they measure visits rather than new customers. As search becomes less dependable, give potential buyers a reason to keep reading your emails and return directly to your site.

founders.title: The New Security Agenda
founders.summary: 87% of 100 surveyed CISOs at companies with more than 1,000 employees expect cybersecurity spending to rise in 2027, yet only 18% run AI SOC tools in production, while 45% plan to buy or upgrade internal AI agent security.

founders.title: Why You Don't Want Humans Doing Outbound Anymore
founders.summary: Agents can run much higher volumes than humans and with better accuracy.

founders.title: Perpetual Motion Machines
founders.summary: Startups can remain unprofitable if each subsidized dollar reduces future costs.

founders.title: Meta's Muse Opportunity in Small Businesses
founders.summary: Meta's consumer reach and SMB relationships could make Muse a hub for business operations and agent-driven shopping.

crypto.title: Strategy's preferred-stock fix sets up renewed bitcoin buying
crypto.summary: MSTR fell nearly 10% after Q3 results and traded at $129.90, down about 27% this year. StoneX and TD Cowen kept buy ratings, with price targets of $435 and $260. Strategy ended the quarter with $5.07B in dollar assets, including a $4.83B cash reserve that covers about 3.2 to 3.4 years of preferred dividends and interest. It spent about $2B buying back its STRC preferred, restoring it near its $100 par value. The cost was bitcoin per share, which is down 3.7% this year. Preferred holders approved daily dividend accrual, effective November 1 for STRC and January 1 for the rest.

crypto.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs see largest daily outflows in four months
crypto.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $643.3M on Friday, the largest outflow since June 25. Spot ether ETFs lost $155.9M, their largest since October 7, and $431.5M for the week. This followed the $6.3B Binance hack, which the FBI attributes to North Korean hackers. Binance saw $3.64B in net outflows in the first nine and a half hours after reopening withdrawals Sunday. Analysts call the ETF move a “sentiment shock” and a de-risking day, since ETF holders have no direct Binance exposure and the outflow was under 1% of ETF assets.

crypto.title: KAST is not launching a token; Points are non-sellable “Pioneer Units”
crypto.summary: Per KAST's own FAQ, eligible Points convert to KAST Pioneer Units, which aren't shares, can't be sold or transferred, and have “no guaranteed cash value,” only a notional value that can rise or fall. Cash-out is only planned, with no dates. Users who miss the in-app acknowledgment deadline in the December update lose their KPUs with no replacement. Eligibility depends on Points balance, KAST balance, and country, and others may get non-withdrawable vouchers for eligible spending. In July, the example was 10,000 Points worth $800 notional, but KAST now gives no conversion rate. Points earning ends November 30, and details come in early December.

crypto.title: PermawebOS: AO Ships 10 Components for Decentralized Computing
crypto.summary: AO shipped 10 components forming PermawebOS, including an Android node runner that bundles for up.arweave[.]net with hardware-backed keys and Verified Boot attestation, inference@1.0 bridging OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and Cerebras with on-device local inference, and QEMU/Docker/andock support for full Linux VM execution inside AO processes. HyperBEAM v0.11 closes 700+ issues with 2x-11x throughput gains, ships LMDB 1.0, and finalizes AO-Core 1.0 alongside hashpaths v2, which introduce ao:// URIs that record full computation provenance for cross-node deduplication and verification. Agents running as AO processes store mailbox, thoughts, and tool policy in on-chain message logs, so no separate runtime holds a private conversation copy, and node TLS certificates bind to the node's Arweave wallet key rather than a traditional CA.

crypto.title: The Crypto End-game: Belief Assets and Cashflow Assets
crypto.summary: Crypto assets are either belief assets (value from shared conviction, no cashflows) and cashflow assets (value from earnings), and token creation is automated but durable demand is not. Belief assets share five structural features: a cult figurehead, a near-death survival that filters for devout holders, early backers made wealthy, a meme-identity layer, and a one-liner rally cry. ZEC qualifies as an emerging belief asset via its shielded-pool vulnerability survival, 30x run, and "private/quantum-proof bitcoin" positioning, with Pearl (PRL) flagged as a possible "AI bitcoin" candidate. The endgame is a two-tier structure: belief assets on top, cashflow assets underneath.

crypto.title: An Asymmetric Bet for Your Institutional Finance Brand
crypto.summary: Five digital asset infrastructure companies pitch to the same fintech founders while ignoring the risk leads, compliance officers, and CTOs who gate institutional deals. The counter-move is niche media positioning: stop publishing about your product and become the searchable reference for your evaluator audience's hardest questions. For a compliant onchain yield infrastructure seller, that means long-form guides and newsletters helping risk teams assess yield integrations, built around lawyers advising fintechs on yield and treasury teams that have shipped integrations. The asymmetric payoff comes from owning one specific question for two or more years while competitors exhaust budget chasing founders who do not decide.

crypto.title: Vitalik Buterin on Digital Minimalism
crypto.summary: Vitalik Buterin published an essay advocating "digital minimalism," the practice of choosing interfaces rather than accepting platform-native defaults. After X's recommendation algorithm surfaced pro-Hitler content and Grok produced antisemitic output in late 2024 and early 2025, he switched to Firefly, a multi-platform client aggregating X, Bluesky, Farcaster, and Lens that bypasses X's algorithmic feed. He reports the switch cut exposure to extremist content and culture-war disputes without requiring him to abandon X. The essay also criticizes "financial nihilism" in crypto circles, the assumption that blockchains trend toward gambling, as a product of the same engagement-optimized information diet warping broader online discourse.

crypto.title: Visa's strongest growth year in more than 15 years
crypto.summary: Visa's FY2026 revenue was $45.9B, up 15%. In Q4, net revenue was $12.1B (+13%), net income $6.0B (+18%), payments volume +9%, cross-border volume +14%, and 74.2B transactions processed (+10%). Other revenue rose 40% to $1.6B. The CEO says “trust” is the next growth vector, backed by a planned $2.4B acquisition of fraud-intelligence company BioCatch.

crypto.summary: Babylon wants to bring native bitcoin collateral to Aave V4.

crypto.summary: HSBC tokenized settlement for Uber on Canton Network captured approximately 1.5 extra days of yield on treasury payments.

crypto.summary: ~$628M in stolen assets were on Tron.

crypto.summary: Coinbase averaged $22B in USDC holdings in Q3, representing 30% of USDC's $73B market cap, and captured roughly 50% of all USDC economics over the past year – its 14th consecutive record quarter, up 49% year-over-year.

it.title: Is Your IT Strategy Ready for the Autonomous Era?
it.summary: 2027 marks a period of software abundance, but running static code will soon give way to orchestrating autonomous machine workers, sensory AI and sovereign limits. The Gartner Top Strategic Technology Trends for 2027 explores three fronts — nontextual AI, autonomous agent platforms and durable agility — to help IT leaders build the boundaries needed for trusted AI outcomes . it.title: OpenAI brings Work features to ChatGPT
it.summary: OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Work capabilities directly into regular Chat while combining usage allowances across ChatGPT and Codex. The changes are intended to simplify access to more advanced workflows and give subscribers greater flexibility in how they use OpenAI's products.

it.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers exposed to active attacks
it.summary: More than 1,000 internet-facing GitLab servers remain vulnerable to a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw that attackers are actively exploiting. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97229, affects GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler and can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

it.title: WorkOS discloses AI-assisted data security incident
it.summary: WorkOS disclosed unauthorized access to an internal sales application on October 30, exposing business contact information, customer account histories, and excerpts from customer communications. The company identified the use of an AI-assisted offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts. It has disabled external access to the affected application while it investigates the full impact.

it.title: Connecting Gemini Enterprise to Snowflake data
it.summary: Google Cloud published a guide demonstrating how to connect Gemini Enterprise agents to Snowflake using the Model Context Protocol and Agent Development Kit. The architecture enables agents to translate natural-language requests into SQL queries through Snowflake Cortex while enforcing user-level permissions and existing data governance controls.

it.title: Are AI certifications still worth it in 2026?
it.summary: The AI certification landscape has shifted as cloud vendors retire older credentials and introduce exams focused on generative AI and agents. Meanwhile, employers are becoming increasingly skeptical of certifications alone, pushing IT professionals to demonstrate practical skills alongside formal credentials.

it.title: AI mandates don't work. Here's what Reddit did instead
it.summary: Top-down directives create activity, not adoption. Learn why Reddit invested in champions and culture instead, and how that approach built lasting momentum. Read how Reddit went from scattered data and misaligned teams to compounding AI ROI with Atlassian in this Enterprise Guide to AI Transformation. Download the guide .

it.title: CrowdStrike and Dell team up to secure enterprise AI
it.summary: CrowdStrike and Dell Technologies announced an integrated security solution for the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, combining AI infrastructure with protection for workloads, agents, and applications. Customers will be able to purchase Dell's AI infrastructure alongside CrowdStrike's Falcon security platform through Dell's AI Ecosystem Program.

it.title: Microsoft and Lumen expand partnership for AI-ready networks
it.summary: Microsoft and Lumen are expanding their collaboration to help enterprises connect data, applications, and infrastructure across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. The companies plan to jointly sell networking solutions and explore bringing additional Lumen capabilities to Azure, simplifying connectivity for enterprise AI workloads and agentic applications.

it.title: Gartner warns enterprises to rethink AI infrastructure
it.summary: Gartner expects AI agents to play a growing role in incident triage, change validation, and IT remediation, but warns that uncontrolled token-based pricing could push costs more than 50% above expectations by 2027. The firm recommends prioritizing measurable use cases, strengthening observability, and preparing hybrid infrastructure for AI workloads.

it.title: Snowflake makes the case for smaller AI models
it.summary: Snowflake argues that enterprises should prioritize intelligence efficiency over deploying the most powerful AI model for every task. Its approach uses model routing to balance performance, latency, and costs, with internal testing showing up to three times greater token efficiency for certain agent workflows without compromising quality.

it.title: Google TPUs are coming to Oracle Cloud
it.summary: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google's TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure starting in 2027, giving enterprises more choices for AI training and inference.

it.title: ServiceNow and OpenAI expand enterprise AI partnership
it.summary: ServiceNow and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to bring governed ServiceNow workflows into ChatGPT and integrate AI capabilities into enterprise security, risk management, and application development.
